desc: Anything not explicitly listed in this RACI is the Customer's responsibility. This includes the underlying cloud account, customer application code, customer-side operational tooling, and any concern not explicitly assigned to Akka in the rows below. The Customer may request additional operational support from Akka via the standard support channel.
Customer owns and operates the account and pays the bill
Customer sets up a dedicated cloud account for Akka to use for hosting the Platform.
Customer ensures enough quota based on usage for compute, storage, etc in the cloud account
Customer executes Terragrunt script to grant programmatic access to the Cloud Account.
The Customer owns the Terraform state backend (cloud storage bucket, locking, encryption) used when running akka-bootstrap. Akka documents the requirements; the Customer runs and secures the backend.

The Customer creates and maintains our permissions into the Cloud Account. Akka has no permissions outside of these and cannot manage any resources or interact with anything in the Cloud Account beyond these. The Customer controls our access and has the ability to cut off access at any time.

For optimal platform management, Akka recommends the use of a dedicated Cloud Account. We further advise against provisioning additional resources in this account to prevent management conflicts. If the Customer decides to add anything outside of this scope, that becomes the Customer responsibility.
Customer reviews and chooses a private connectivity pattern from the supported AAO patterns. Akka reviews and validates feasibility.
AAO installs a load balancer for the region and configures a certificate issuer (Let's Encrypt by default). This certificate provider is used for platform APIs and generated application hostnames.

act: Ingress/Egress Connectivity using private patterns with auto autogenerated IP address
desc: AAO installs the region using the Customer's chosen private connectivity option. A load balancer is provisioned for the region with an automatically generated IP address, ensuring internal communication without traversing the public internet.

act: IP Address Management cidr range allocation
desc: Customer assigns an appropriately sized CIDR block for cases where peering or hub and spoke is desired.

act: VPC Peering or Hub and Spoke enablement (Not available on all cloud providers)
desc: Customer sets up VPC peering or hub and spoke enablement.
The Customer is responsible for setting up and maintaining the IP allowlist for NAT gateways and load balancer.
Customer creates and maintains DNS records for platform machinery and apps in the cloud provider DNS zones configured by Akka for the installation.
Akka publishes a whitepaper and implementation details for the private connectivity patterns available on each cloud provider, which the Customer reviews when selecting a connectivity pattern.
The Customer reviews Akka's default networking, compute, and persistence configuration, and recommends changes to improve app performance, optimize costs, or address other concerns.
Akka installs the Teleport identity-aware proxy that is used for federation.
Akka uses Teleport for human access to platform infrastructure, with session recording and audit logging. Access requires explicit justification and approval per Akka's Access Control Policy.
The Customer identifies region groups based on their use case and informs Akka.
Akka configures region groups on the Federation Plane based on the Customer's region groups configuration

act: Provide maintenance window, usually 1-4 hours per week.
desc: The maintenance window is used by Akka for any operation that may cause downtime, including database minor updates (applied automatically by the cloud provider) and manual upgrades such as database major patches.

Akka manages infrastructure patching and vulnerability remediation for the Platform, including the JVM, the container base image, the operating system, and the Akka runtime that ship with the customer's deployed services. Vulnerability reports are available from Akka's trust center.
The Customer should provide a maintenance window. Akka will notify the Customer prior to any maintenance that causes downtime.
Akka schedules regular releases to installations, which can include the Runtime, Region machinery, and Federation Plane.

Customer periodically reviews their cloud account subscription and the monthly charges that are incurred. Akka auto-provisions and maintains the cloud infrastructure and overhead required to run an Akka region. Automatic provisioning and de-provisioning of compute instances to accommodate utilization demand. Automatic scaling of underlying persistence stores to accommodate concurrency demand. Akka has various sizing options to keep costs in check but HA is the default.

Scaling of compute instances and underlying persistence stores. Akka monitors utilization and concurrency demand and auto-scales accordingly within Akka's defined sizing standards. The Customer should notify Akka in advance if they expect rapid expansion or need pre-warming for performance testing or spiky loads.
Akka dynamically adds and removes compute and persistence to accommodate real-time traffic against the Customer's performance SLA targets.

When the Customer requests removal of a Region (e.g., end of contract, scope change, or topology adjustment), Akka follows the documented decommissioning runbook to gracefully remove the Region from the Federation Plane and clean up stale resources.
The Customer submits feature requests via the support channel. Akka triages, prioritizes, and communicates status.
If any suspicious SIEM alerts are found, please notify Akka.
The Customer creates and maintains the key material for the CMEK and shares its identifier with Akka. Customer is responsible for ensuring access to the CMEK

Where Akka cannot automatically provision TLS certificates (e.g., private load balancers, or where the Customer brings its own domain), the Customer provides certificates or configures cert-manager. Akka validates and deploys. See https://doc.akka.io/operations/tls-certificates.html#_custom_server_certificates for details.
Akka monitors all Platform logs except for SDK logs.

Akka monitors and reports availability of the Akka Platform, with uptime reports available on request. Platform availability commitments are governed by the Akka Federation Plane SLA Policy. Availability of customer-deployed services running on the platform is the Customer's responsibility; see the Services category.
Akka monitors metrics and logs and will notify the Customer as needed.

act: Akka Region Platform Telemetry for the Customer (optional)
desc: Customer can optionally choose to set up platform telemetry for the cluster and for the database instance as they own the account. Akka can be consulted for components that they can set up observability
The Customer configures export of application logs and metrics to its observability platform via Akka SDK integration patterns.
Akka enables scheduled database backups and notifies the Customer once configured.
The Customer notifies Akka after taking ad-hoc database backups (e.g., before high-risk changes, or snapshots taken for incident handling).
Akka uses Velero to back up stateful Kubernetes resources for point-in-time recovery.
Akka performs periodic restore testing against backups; results are summarized on request. The Disaster Recovery Exercise row covers joint exercises.
Akka and the Customer work together periodically to simulate a disaster and fully recover from it, ensuring the recovery meets or exceeds the Customer's needs.
The Customer specifies replication mode (e.g., region-pinned, replicated) per service. Akka enables and operates the underlying replication.
Akka provides tooling and runbooks for failover. The Customer is consulted before failover and informed of execution.
Akka publishes default RTO/RPO. Customer-specific targets can be agreed where Akka's standard does not meet the Customer's needs.

The Customer owns and operates the SDLC environment used to build services running on Akka, including IDE choices, source code repository, CI/CD pipelines, and developer programming environments. Akka ships developer tooling that the Customer integrates into the SDLC: IDE AI assistants, a local development environment, unit and integration testing utilities, and deployment configuration / deployment tooling.
Customer runs akka-bootstrap which sets up IAM for the cloud account where the region is installed
Akka delivers quarterly access-control reports for the Customer's installation. Database-level audit logging is also available where required.
Akka creates and manages the service accounts, service account keys, and IAM bindings required for Platform operation within the Customer's cloud account.

Akka uses Teleport for human access to platform infrastructure, with session recording and audit logging. Access requires explicit justification and approval per Akka's Access Control Policy. Teleport audit logs are available to the Customer on request.

Where access to customer-confidential data is required (e.g., for incident handling), Akka requests authorization per the Access Control for Customer-Confidential Data policy. Audit logs of such access are available to the Customer on request.
The Customer's IDP enforces MFA for users accessing Akka console and CLI. Akka enforces MFA on its own internal access.

Customer is responsible for how services handle PII and to ensure such handling is compliant with GDPR or other applicable privacy regulations. Akka acts as neither controller nor processor of data handled by the Customer's services.

Akka Federation Plane integrates with the Customer's identity provider to manage organizations, users, and team access controls. Application-level access scoping is handled separately via ACLs and tokens (see Services, Security, Service ACLs).
The Customer provides enterprise identity, authentication, and authorization systems and policies.
Akka maintains uptime for the Federation Plane and configures disaster recovery for it.

At onboarding, Akka and the Customer agree on operational and engagement-level communication channels for routine collaboration (e.g., shared Slack channels, email distribution lists, regular review cadence). Formal support and incident channels are governed separately by the Customer Support Policy and the Incident Response row.

Akka provides 24/7 incident response per the Customer Support Policy. The Customer opens incidents through the Customer Support Portal (support.akka.io), Akka Console (console.akka.io/support), or by email to support@akka.io. Severity classifications, response time SLOs, escalation procedures, and incident communication protocols follow Akka's Customer Support Policy and Incident Management Process. Other shared channels (e.g., Slack) may exist for ongoing engagements but are not a substitute for formal support cases.
cad: Per Customer Support Policy: Severity 1 initial response within 1 hour (24/7); Severity 2 within 4 business hours. Subsequent updates per Incident Management Process.

desc: Akka delivers post-incident reviews for Severity 1 and 2 incidents within an agreed cadence following resolution.

Akka notifies the Customer in advance of planned maintenance windows that could affect availability, and via release notify emails for runtime/SDK releases. Maintenance windows should be set in advance by the Customer.
Recurring operational review covering system health, maintenance, incidents, and roadmap items relevant to the Customer.
Periodic alignment session covering usage, capacity, product direction, and Customer priorities.
Executive-level partnership review covering relationship health, escalation status, and strategic items.
Joint onboarding covering account setup, Region provisioning, connectivity validation, and acceptance criteria.
Customers sign up for Portal access, Akka assigns their Region and walks them through console and CLI usage, and ticketing flow.
The Customer manages its own users, teams, and role assignments within the Akka console.
At end of contract, Akka coordinates region decommission, return or destruction of customer data, and revocation of access per the Data Retention Policy.
Akka tracks Customer-raised issues and remediation through to closure with status visibility to the Customer.
Akka responds to Customer CAIQ/SIG and bespoke security questionnaires drawing on the ISMS control library.
Akka notifies the Customer without undue delay where a breach of Akka-held customer data poses risk, including nature, scope, and remediation.
Customer organizations are screened against sanctions lists periodically. The Customer is informed if a screening result requires action.
Akka provides advance notice of any planned product or feature EOL with sufficient lead time for migration planning.

act: Encryption in Transit and at Rest
desc: Akka encrypts customer data in transit (TLS) and at rest using cloud provider encryption services. Default keys are Akka-managed.

Lifecycle, rotation, and access control of cryptographic materials follow the Akka Key Management and Cryptography Policy. Cloud-native KMS handles lifecycle for Akka-managed materials. Customer-managed keys (CMEK, BYO certificates) are managed by the Customer per the same policy.
cad: Per Key Management and Cryptography Policy

desc: Akka performs continuous vulnerability scanning of platform components and dependencies; findings are tracked to remediation per the Vulnerability Management Policy. Customers are notified of critical and high severity security patches via security advisory emails and the trust center. Disclosure occurs no later than the date the patch is made available, with coordinated advance notice to affected customers where applicable.
Akka performs background checks on personnel with access to customer environments and provides security awareness training, per the Personnel Security Policy.
Akka maintains SOC 2 Type II for the Akka Platform. Report available under NDA via trust.akka.io. SOC 3 is also available as a publicly-shareable companion.

Customer data is stored within the cloud region(s) configured for the customer's installation. Multi-region installations replicate within customer-selected regions only. Each customer's data is isolated in dedicated database resources; no shared data plane across customers.
Akka is responsible for securing all customer data located within the Federation Plane.
The Customer is responsible for securing Federation Plane tokens and access to projects.
The Federation Plane does not handle customer data; it processes only minimal PII consisting of customer user and administrator identities, in accordance with Akka's GDPR-compliant privacy policy.
Current subprocessor list maintained at trust.akka.io.
Annual third-party penetration testing conducted as part of SOC 2 audit cycle. Executive summary available under NDA via trust.akka.io.

Akka maintains audit logs of control-plane actions (e.g., authentication, project and service lifecycle, IAM and token changes). Logs delivered on request. Recurring delivery cadences can also be arranged.

act: Application code & dependency patching / Vulnerability management
desc: The Customer reviews their application code and any libraries or dependencies they introduce for security issues and vulnerabilities. The JVM, container base image, OS, and Akka runtime packaged into the deployed service are patched by Akka (see Platform / Maintenance / Infrastructure patch / Vulnerability management).
The Customer configures services to enable their functionality, including secrets for accessing other services.
Where services depend on integrations such as brokers or object storage, the Customer configures these for the Akka Project before service deployment.
The Customer owns and manages the lifecycle of Akka SDK apps.
Source code management for Akka Service implementations is the Customer's responsibility.
The Customer controls service instance counts within configured limits.

act: Logs from Services Built with Akka SDK
desc: Metrics and logs are sent to the Customer's logging platform. Akka filters out logs at the source so they are not sent to Akka's internal observability stack.
The Customer monitors application logs.
The Customer can configure dashboards over cloud security logs and stream them to a GSOC or observability tool.
The Customer configures Service ACLs to protect access to non-public service endpoints.
Akka SDK supports access scoping through JWTs and JWKS.
